mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-16.4 to -14.9), indicating a self-reinforcing recovery in discretionary shopping and leisure activity. This momentum is expected to persist, pushing the next-4-week mean of RETAIL_REC above the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -16.4 to -14.9 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to continue its upward trajectory and instead reverses to a lower 4-week mean despite the observed 3-week uptrend, rejecting pure momentum continuation.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has been volatile and remains deeply negative (-17.4 to -14.4). If TRANSIT's trailing 2-week mean falls below -15 points, reduced transit-enabled trip-chaining to shopping districts will suppress RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT trailing 2-week mean falls below -15 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranged between -11.6 and -17.4 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next two weeks even after TRANSIT's trailing 2-week mean crosses below -15 points.

The interaction effect is stronger than either series acting alone because commuting restores both transit infrastructure use and daytime foot traffic near retail corridors.

evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES recovered from -25.6 to -17.7 then dipped to -21.3, showing volatility rather than sustained joint increase
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean declines or stays flat even when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together in the same week, indicating no synergistic commuting effect.

mechanism_narrative: The decision date of 2021-11-15 falls within the pre-holiday shopping ramp-up period. Regardless of short-term fluctuations in other mobility categories, calendar-driven holiday shopping behavior structurally increases retail and recreation visits over the following four weeks.

When PARKS spikes more than 10 points above the prior week, outdoor recreation substitutes for indoor retail and recreation trips, temporarily depressing RETAIL_REC the following week.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -7.1 to 7.6 in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a PARKS spike greater than 10 points, refuting the substitution effect.
